primitives.name: Sustainable Throughput
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **Sustainable throughput:** the maximum ingestion rate a system sustains without large latency fluctuations — measured by controlling the driver's ingestion rate rather than letting systems ingest at max rate (which just measures backpressure collapse).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'lambda_in': 'Ingestion rate (events/s)', 'epsilon': 'Prescribed threshold for acceptable latency fluctuation'}
primitives.assumptions: Driver controls input rate; system operates in steady-state without backpressure collapse.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Backpressure collapse at maximum achievable throughput.

layer2.mapping: GSE: The "sustainable throughput" of the serving layer is the maximum request arrival rate it can handle while maintaining p99 latency below the operational threshold. GSI: For conformal prediction, this maps to the maximum volume of historical data the calibration engine can process within the deadline without degrading coverage accuracy.
layer2.telemetry: Measured by gradually increasing driver injection rate until p99 latency begins to degrade sharply.

primitives.name: Event-Time Latency
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Latency definition for stateful operators:** event-time latency = source production timestamp → sink result emission, measured externally in the driver (prior work measured inside the SUT, hiding backpressure).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_emit': 'Timestamp of sink result emission (s)', 't_source': 'Production timestamp of the source event (s)'}
primitives.assumptions: External driver timestamps events; latency includes all processing delay including backpressure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Latency spikes when system is overloaded.

layer2.mapping: GSE: Event-time latency is the end-to-end delay from request reception to response emission, accounting for all internal queuing and processing. GSI: In conformal inference, it is the wall-clock time from ingesting a new observation to emitting a prediction interval.
layer2.telemetry: End-to-end latency time series, especially p99/p99.9 fractiles.

primitives.name: Skew Stress Test
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Workload tuning per system documented honestly: Spark 4s batch size, Storm workers/executors/buffer tuning, Flink network-bound at 4+ nodes; Storm's backpressure immature (dropped queue connections at high load = treated as failure).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Single hot key dominates resource consumption, causing cascading failures.

layer2.mapping: GSE: Simulate Super Bowl traffic or a viral esports match where one game or user group generates 80% of requests. GSI: Test if a single feature category (e.g., player position) causes disproportionate computational load in the calibration pipeline.
layer2.telemetry: Latency quantiles (p95/p99) for the skewed key versus the average.

primitives.name: Fluctuation Stress Test
primitives.verbatim_quote: Assumptions: on-the-fly generation is faithful to production feeds; the gaming workloads generalize to other streaming analytics; per-system tuning effort was comparable (authors disclose the tuning surface per engine).
primitives.assumptions: Workload varies over time following a known pattern.
primitives.breakdown_regime: System fails to adapt quickly enough to sudden changes.

layer2.mapping: GSE: Replay historical traffic traces with realistic burst patterns (e.g., pre-game to post-game surges) to ensure the serving layer handles ramp-up and ramp-down without service disruptions. GSI: Verify that the model retraining pipeline can cope with intermittent bursts of fresh data without compromising online prediction quality.
layer2.telemetry: Latency during transitions and recovery time to settle back to baseline.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that traditional benchmarks measuring "peak throughput" are misleading because they ignore the critical role of backpressure and fluctuation robustness. A system that saturates at maximum rate will exhibit catastrophic latency variance, which is unacceptable for real-time applications like sports betting. Sustainable throughput defines the operating envelope where the system behaves deterministically, decoupling the driver from the SUT. Event-time latency provides an external, verifiable metric that exposes hidden backpressure in the system. Skew and fluctuation tests reveal fundamental architectural weaknesses: Storm's immature backpressure caused connection drops, indicating a lack of flow control. These primitives form a minimal test suite that captures the essential performance and reliability requirements of a modern serving layer.
